1. packages/plugin-rsc/examples/browser-mode2 (entire PR) — The PR author's own checklist states the example is non-functional: `node:async_hosts` fails to resolve in the browser RSC environment and the polyfill doesn't work, so the example never actually renders RSC output. Shipping a broken example under `examples/` misleads users copying it as a working reference. Fix: do not merge until the RSC environment actually runs end-to-end in the browser (resolve or properly alias Node built-ins used transitively by react-server-dom/React, or document that this is a known limitation and gate the example accordingly); otherwise hold the PR until `node:async_hooks` resolution is solved.

2. packages/plugin-rsc/examples/browser-mode2/vite.config.ts (`/@vite/invoke-rsc` middleware) — The RSC invoke payload is taken straight from a GET query string (`JSON.parse(url.searchParams.get('data'))`) and dispatched to `server.environments['rsc'].hot.handleInvoke`, with no origin/referrer check. This opens an arbitrary RPC-invoke endpoint reachable by any page (CSRF-style, since it's a simple GET) that can drive the dev server's module runner. Fix: mirror whatever origin/method checks the existing `browser-mode` example's module-runner-invoke endpoint uses (e.g. require POST, check `Origin`/`sec-fetch-site`), rather than accepting unauthenticated cross-origin GETs.

3. packages/plugin-rsc/examples/browser-mode2/vite.config.ts (`load` for build mode) — The production loader does `import("/dist/rsc/index.js")` from the client bundle, i.e. it has the client ship a dynamic import of server-side RSC build output into the browser. This both contradicts "no Node server required" framing (the RSC bundle presumably still needs Node built-ins resolved) and is unvalidated/untested — there's no indication `pnpm build && pnpm preview` was actually run successfully. Fix: verify the build path works, or remove/guard it until it does; don't leave an untested code path presented as supported ("## Build" section in README).

4. packages/plugin-rsc/examples/browser-mode2/README.md — Describes HMR support, server actions, and a full working architecture as shipped features, but the PR's own checklist says the example doesn't load past the `async_hooks` failure. The README is aspirational/inaccurate documentation for a broken example. Fix: either mark the example clearly as WIP/broken (e.g. a top banner stating the known limitation) or hold the README claims until the feature works.

5. Scope/policy — This PR is submitted with an explicitly incomplete, self-acknowledged non-working state ("Copilot's incomplete work" checklist, "Need to resolve" section left in the description). Per normal maintainer convention, PRs adding a new example package (with its own `package.json`, lockfile entries, CI surface) should not be merged while admittedly broken. Fix: convert to draft and keep open until the blocking `async_hooks` resolution issue is solved, or close in favor of a follow-up once a working approach is found.

6. pnpm-lock.yaml / package.json — Adds a whole new example package (new deps, new lockfile entries) purely to host currently-nonfunctional code. This increases CI matrix/install cost for zero working payload. Fix: hold off adding the package (and its lockfile diff) until the example is functional, rather than merging infrastructure for a broken demo.
